content: Cefuroxime is a cephalosporin antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. It is not effective against viral infections such as the common cold or flu. This medication should be taken orally as directed by your doctor, typically twice daily (every 12 hours). To improve absorption and reduce stomach upset, take cefuroxime with food. Swallow the tablets whole; do not crush or chew them, as they have a strong bitter taste. For optimal results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals and complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or stomach pain. Dizziness and drowsiness may occur, particularly with higher doses. Rarely, this medication can cause a severe intestinal condition due to the bacteria Clostridium difficile (C. diff), which may occur during treatment or weeks to months after stopping the medication. Prolonged or repeated use of cefuroxime may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions are rare but possible. Before taking cefuroxime, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, penicillins, or other cephalosporin antibiotics (e.g., cephalexin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Cefuroxime may cause dizziness or drowsiness, and alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Cefuroxime may interfere with live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine), reducing their effectiveness. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It passes into breast milk, but the risk to a nursing infant is considered low. Discuss the benefits and risks with your doctor. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Cefuroxime may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., diabetic urine tests, blood glucose tests), potentially causing false results. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. In case of overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it later for another infection unless directed by your doctor. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
